what: Times of the sky events the site prints, solved on NASA JPL Horizons (DE441). Each row keeps the NASA instant (UTC, to the second) and the engine instants it replaces, as the committed data files record them.

provenance.quantity: apparent geocentric ecliptic longitude of date (OBSERVER table, QUANTITIES 31, CENTER 500@399, APPARENT AIRLESS, EXTRA_PREC YES)
provenance.timeScale: TIME_TYPE UT: UTC from 1962, UT1 before
provenance.targets: Sun 10, Mercury 199, Venus 299, system barycentres 4 to 9 for Mars to Pluto
provenance.method: nine-point Lagrange interpolation of each table, roots by bisection to 1e-9 day (scripts/accuracy-audit/truth.py, docs/engine-validation/independent-references/tools/series.py); instants rounded to the second

withinOneMinute.note: Left out of the table: the engine already places these within a minute of NASA
withinOneMinute.lunations: every new and full Moon agrees with NASA to the second (docs/accuracy-audit-2026-11/REPORT.md)
withinOneMinute.moonIngresses: every Moon sign change agrees with NASA to the second (docs/accuracy-audit-2026-11/REPORT.md)
